contract: Sparse chain summaries begin at the retained canonical low point, advance by (realHigh-low+2)/2, end at the tip, and contain at most 30 IDs.
The highest summary ID still on the canonical chain is the common block.
ChainInventory contains the common block followed by at most 2000 consecutive successors; remain is the exact unsent height count.
Responses require request correlation, 1..2001 IDs, at least 2000 IDs when remain is nonzero, a requested first ID, consecutive heights, and a bounded future terminal height.
Fetch scheduling is ordered and bounded to 500 global and 100 per peer; timed-out requests are eligible for retry without being treated as unsolicited duplicates.
Network block bytes pass unchanged to C019 RawBlock/BlockManager; C011 Khaos remains the sole fork graph and no network consensus implementation is introduced.
